questions.stemEn: A patient has recurrent fractures, hearing loss and blue sclerae. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: Recurrent fractures + hearing loss + blue sclerae هي clues التي يستخدمها المصدر لـosteogenesis imperfecta.
questions.reasoningEn: The phenotype is classic for osteogenesis imperfecta in the source.
questions.clinicalPearl: OI is a collagen disorder; phenotype and severity vary by type.

tts.text: A patient has recurrent fractures, hearing loss and blue sclerae. What is the most likely diagnosis? A. Osteogenesis imperfecta.

questions.stemEn: A full-term newborn has blue sclerae and an abnormal body-bone X-ray in the provided image. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار osteogenesis imperfecta اعتمادًا على blue sclerae مع skeletal X-ray abnormalities.
questions.reasoningEn: The recalled diagnosis depends on blue sclerae plus the provided skeletal radiograph.
questions.clinicalPearl: The radiograph is part of the diagnostic clue and must remain attached to the question.

questions.stemEn: A 2-year-old girl has had two fractures and was investigated for child abuse. Her mother has poor hearing and tooth decay. There is no family history of short stature. What is the possible cause of recurrent fractures?
questions.explanationAr: Maternal hearing problems وdental abnormalities مع recurrent fractures في الطفلة تدعم inherited osteogenesis imperfecta في مفتاح المصدر.
questions.reasoningEn: The family history of hearing and dental abnormalities supports osteogenesis imperfecta over nutritional disease or abuse in the source vignette.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Rickets وvitamin C deficiency تحتاج clues غذائية/مخبرية مختلفة، وchild abuse لا يفسر family phenotype المذكور.
questions.clinicalPearl: OI and non-accidental injury can overlap clinically; evaluate the full history, fracture pattern and phenotype carefully.

What is the possible cause of recurrent fractures? A. Rickets. B. Vitamin C deficiency. C. Osteogenesis imperfecta. D. Child abuse.

questions.stemEn: A 2-year-old girl has recurrent fractures with a family history suggesting osteogenesis imperfecta. What is the best way to establish the diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار molecular testing، خصوصًا COL1A1/COL1A2، كmainstay لتأكيد osteogenesis imperfecta.
questions.reasoningEn: The source states that molecular analysis of OI-associated genes is the diagnostic mainstay.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Skeletal survey يصف injuries والعظام لكنه لا يحدد molecular diagnosis، وvitamin D يفيد differential، وbone biopsy ليس first-line في المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Genetic testing should be interpreted alongside phenotype and family history.

tts.text: A two-year-old girl has recurrent fractures with a family history suggesting osteogenesis imperfecta. What is the best way to establish the diagnosis? A. DNA testing. B. Bone biopsy. C. Skeletal survey. D. Vitamin D level.

questions.stemEn: A 2-month-old infant has left mandibular swelling without fever. Cultures are negative and head CT is suggestive of Caffey disease. How should the child be managed?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار indomethacin ويذكر أن prednisone قد يُستخدم عند poor response. لأن management قد يختلف حسب شدة الحالة، نحتفظ بمفتاح المصدر مع التحقق لاحقًا.
questions.reasoningEn: The source lists indomethacin as treatment for infantile cortical hyperostosis, with prednisone if response is poor.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Vancomycin لا يناسب الحالة مع negative cultures وradiologic Caffey pattern. Cortisone ليس المفتاح الأول في المصدر.
questions.clinicalPearl: Mandibular involvement is a useful clue distinguishing Caffey disease from some other causes of infant bone swelling.

questions.stemEn: An infant with a large head, short limbs and neck, and broad forehead has achondroplasia. What is the most common cause of death among the listed options?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار cervico-medullary compression ويذكر أنه يرتبط significant morbidity/mortality وsudden infant death risk في achondroplasia.
questions.reasoningEn: The source identifies cervicomedullary compression as the major mortality risk among the listed choices.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: OSA مهم سريريًا لكنه ليس مفتاح المصدر. Lumbar stenosis أكثر ارتباطًا بمضاعفات لاحقة وليس السبب المختار للوفاة هنا.
questions.clinicalPearl: Infants with achondroplasia require attention to foramen-magnum/cervicomedullary compression and sleep-disordered breathing.

questions.stemEn: A child has ocular telangiectasia as shown. Which of the following could be the cause of this presentation?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يجيب 'chromosomal abnormality' ثم يشرح Ataxia-telangiectasia كgenome/chromosomal instability/DNA-repair disorder. لفظ الخيار واسع وغير دقيق، لذلك نحفظه كـrecall فقط.
questions.reasoningEn: The source links the ocular telangiectasia to ataxia-telangiectasia but uses a broad option label, 'chromosomal abnormality.'
questions.clinicalPearl: Ataxia-telangiectasia is a DNA-damage response/genome-instability syndrome; the source option wording is imprecise.

questions.stemEn: A child has ocular telangiectasia, recurrent infections and siblings with the same disease. Which laboratory finding is expected?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يربط الحالة بـAtaxia-telangiectasia، ومن laboratory features المذكورة elevated AFP.
questions.reasoningEn: Elevated AFP is a common laboratory feature of ataxia-telangiectasia in the source explanation.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: High uric acid، high calcium وhigh CK ليست العلامة التي يختارها المصدر لهذه الحالة.
questions.clinicalPearl: A-T combines progressive neurologic disease, telangiectasia, immune dysfunction and increased malignancy risk.

questions.stemEn: A 10-year-old girl has telangiectasia on the eyes and ear pinna with frequent nosebleeds. She is a good student and active in soccer. Her sister died from the same problem. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanationAr: المصدر يختار Osler-Weber-Rendu syndrome. Frequent epistaxis + visible telangiectasia + positive family history fit hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia more than Ataxia-telangiectasia، خصوصًا أن الطفلة جيدة دراسيًا ورياضيًا دون ataxia مذكورة.
questions.reasoningEn: The source uses mucocutaneous telangiectasia, recurrent epistaxis and family history to favor hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
questions.incorrectOptionsAr: Ataxia-telangiectasia عادةً تتضمن progressive ataxia/neurologic findings وimmune problems، وVWD لا يفسر telangiectatic lesions العائلية بهذا النمط.
questions.clinicalPearl: Family history plus spontaneous recurrent epistaxis and telangiectasia are core clues to HHT.
